I faced this issue running OpenCode through SSH on a remote Ubuntu server—I was unable to authenticate Notion MCP due to the 127.0.0.1 redirect URL.

A workaround is after you complete authentication in the host browser, copy the`/callback` URL from the browser and use `curl` on the remote machine to complete the OAuth flow (where `127.0.0.1` can be resolved).

```bash
# On the machine running `opencode mcp auth`
curl "http://127.0.0.1:19876/whatever-is-in-browser-url-bar..."
```

Hopefully the PR mentioned above will make this more streamlined!

This was fixed in commit 7e681b0bc ("fix(app): large text pasted into prompt-input causes main thread lock"). The fix optimizes the prompt-input parsing by avoiding unnecessary regex replacements on every buffer flush, short-circuiting text joining for single-part inputs, and using a fast regex test instead of allocating a trimmed string for the empty-check. These changes eliminate the main-thread lock when pasting large text.

It seems unlikely this issue is caused by OpenCode - there are reports from other users experiencing the same with other tools via OpenRouter.

Since these issues affect both providers on two different platforms (OpenRouter and OpenCode) I have reached out to both Moonshot and MiniMax to try to get to the bottom of this.

> Which is the core issue regarding adding Agent Team mode?

Honestly, the core issue is speed. One model doing everything sequentially feels sluggish. I'd love to see multiple agents run in parallel—like one writing code while another plans the next steps—to make the whole workflow faster.

I don't want this to sound rude but this felt like such a big oversight I honestly thought `/share` was broken and had to come digging through issues.

I love so much about OpenCode but this makes sharing multiple message conversations with desktop users unintuitive, especially non-technicals.

The current controls are: 

1. Small so easy to miss,
2. Quite low contrast,
3. Unlabelled/unexplaiend

I understand this [works as one would expect on mobile](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/10032) but not desktop... Why? :)

Otherwise, could we have next/previous buttons that are larger, clearly and centrally located under the message (above the footer)? That would at least help if we absolutely must have only one message at a time.
